content:
There are prior audit reports, but I should focus on my own analysis of the current code since that's what was asked, mentioning past reports only briefly. I'm planning to fan out exploration across distinct areas to trace how a request reaches a model, starting with the core shared runtime files handling providers, model aliases, and AI service config.

Beyond that, I need to map the handlers (gpt.go, gemini.go, azure_openai.go, and various quiz/research/transcription endpoints) to see which client path each uses, plus the offline/CLI generators. Given the scale (~60k lines), I'll delegate parallel exploration for the handlers and generators while reading the core abstractions myself.

Actually, since delegated searches shouldn't overlap with my own, I'll split cleanly: agents cover handlers, offline tools, and the core runtime, while I separately do a quick cross-cutting grep for raw HTTP call sites to AI endpoints to measure how many places bypass the SDK abstractions. I want the agent prompts to return specific file:line references for each call site, along with which provider and transport (raw net/http, genai SDK, eino, genkit, ADK, or OpenRouter) is being used.

For each call site I also want model selection source, credentials/endpoint origin, retry/fallback and timeout behavior, streaming support, logging, billing labels, moderation, and error sanitization — plus flagging duplicated helpers like multiple Azure or Gemini clients and repeated JSON repair logic. I'll exclude the worktrees directory and underscore-prefixed files since those are ignored by the Go build and effectively dead code, though I should note their existence.
